parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the prompt requirements: Rust 2021, same CLI/default behavior, exact algorithm and stdout formatting, zero external crates, a Cargo project, root test11.rs, and black-box inference from the compiled executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept ownership of implementation, integration, building, and acceptance. It spawned one child only to probe formatting details while the parent continued its own black-box probes and later used the returned formatting findings.
parallel.implementation: The parent added Cargo.toml, test11.rs, and src/lib.rs, src/rgb.rs, src/converter.rs, and src/formatting.rs. The implementation used f32 arithmetic, channelwise inversion, Rec.709 grayscale weights, custom cout-style formatting, and abort-like parse failure behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent assembled the Cargo package and standalone root entry file in /output, then produced a direct /output/test11 executable and release build artifacts listed by artifact validation.
parallel.verification: The parent compiled with cargo build --release and rustc test11.rs -O -o test11, compared outputs against /workspace/dataset/test11_executable on representative and edge cases, and the official evaluator later passed 40/40.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished required behavior is evidenced at closure. The official evaluation completed successfully and no child result or implementation artifact was left pending.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same Rust 2021, CLI, formatting, dependency, project layout, black-box, and output requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single parent agent owned every stage: probing the reference executable, writing root-level modules and test11.rs, fixing build and behavior defects, rebuilding, validating, and delivering.
serial.implementation: The serial agent created Cargo.toml, lib.rs, color.rs, cli.rs, format.rs, and test11.rs. It implemented f32 color conversion, std::stof-style prefix parsing, cout-like default float formatting, and then fixed the module path and negative-NaN sign handling.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial agent integrated all files in one workspace, corrected the import path so both Cargo and direct rustc builds worked, and delivered both /output/test11 and target/release/test11.
serial.verification: The serial agent ran sample checks, built with Cargo and rustc, tried a Python harness but found Python unavailable, switched to shell, found and fixed -nan behavior, and then validated 523 deterministic and random cases byte-for-byte.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished required behavior is evidenced at closure. The final shell parity check passed and the official evaluator passed 40/40.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the exact migration obligations, especially same CLI defaults, f32-style logic, byte-for-byte stdout, std-only Rust, Cargo structure, and root test11.rs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial operated from the same prompt and likewise recognized exact CLI behavior, formatting, no external dependencies, project layout, and build requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference affected the official outcome; both covered the required behavior and passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split only the formatting investigation to a child while the parent owned implementation, integration, build, and final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation or child activity; the single agent owned probing, writing, integration, and validation end to end.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained an auxiliary probe handoff, but did not fragment implementation ownership; serial solved the same work locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child received a narrow formatting-probe task, returned findings on CLI semantics, f32 math, grayscale weights, and cout formatting, and the parent continued with a custom formatter plan.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no handoff boundary; it inferred formatting and math directly through local reference-executable probes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a context boundary, but the boundary carried the needed information back and there is no conflicting, stale, lossy, or overloaded handoff consequence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a small src module tree plus root test11.rs and implemented conversion plus custom formatting in one parent-owned patch.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote root-level module files and then patched cli.rs after a module path error and later patched NaN sign parsing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The file layout and repair path differed, but both implementations converged on the same tested behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The one child completed and its final answer reached the parent before the parent wrote and tested the solution.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join; all results were local command outputs consumed directly by the agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an additional child-result lifecycle, but it was returned and used; serial avoided the lifecycle entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Only the parent wrote the implementation workspace; the child supplied findings and did not produce files to merge or overwrite.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The single serial agent wrote and patched all files itself in one workspace, including the later cli.rs fix.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no harmful shared-state interaction in parallel; serial had ordinary self-repairs rather than cross-agent collisions.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built with Cargo and rustc, then ran parity checks against the C++ executable on defaults, partial args, special values, signed zero, rounding boundaries, and error-path behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built with Cargo and rustc, validated sample outputs, switched from unavailable Python to shell, found a -nan mismatch, fixed it, and reran 523 comparison cases with no mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial performed a broader final local parity sweep and fixed one extra edge case; both nevertheless satisfied the official evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed in about 203 agent seconds without timeout, closed after builds and parity checks, and official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 314 agent seconds without timeout, closed after a broader shell parity run, and official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used less recorded agent time and one child; serial spent longer but remained within budget. Neither left deadline-displaced work.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluator records show no discordant outcome: both parallel and serial passed 40/40. The concrete difference is process shape, not success: parallel delegated the risky formatting probe to one child and then parent-implemented a src-based project, while serial performed all probing locally, wrote root-level modules, fixed two ordinary implementation defects, and performed a broader local final comparison.
parallel_contributors: A narrow child formatting probe returned usable findings before implementation.
The parent retained implementation, build, validation, and final delivery ownership.
serial_contributors: The single agent independently probed formatting and CLI behavior.
The serial agent fixed an import-path build error and a -nan parsing mismatch before final validation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used src/ modules while serial used root-level modules.
Serial encountered and fixed ordinary local code defects that were not caused by parallel coordination.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; both official evaluations passed and no retained parallel coordination failure is needed to explain the result

There were no incompatible child reports or unresolved contracts; one formatting handoff aligned with the parent's own probes.
